query: For the paper "Exploring Domain Shift in Extractive Text Summarization" (arXiv: 1908.11664), answer this question: What settings did they experiment with?

drafts: They experimented under three evaluation settings: IN-DOMAIN, OUT-OF-DOMAIN, and CROSS-DATASET, which allow evaluating both the quality of domain-aware text representation and adaptation to unfamiliar domains [1]. Experiments were performed mainly on their multi-domain MULTI-SUM dataset [6]. Source domains are defined as the first five domains in Table 1 (IN-DOMAIN), while the other domains (OUT-OF-DOMAIN) are totally invisible during training; IN-DOMAIN tests learning different domain distributions on a multi-domain set, and OUT-OF-DOMAIN tests performance on unseen domains [6]. They investigated four learning strategies for dealing with domain shift under these three settings [2][1], and additionally designed a simple analytical experiment on the MULTI-SUM dataset where they take turns choosing one domain and train the basic model on its training data to verify the existence of domain shift [3].

requirements.reason: 答案完整覆盖了论文的三种实验设置（IN-DOMAIN、OUT-OF-DOMAIN、CROSS-DATASET）、实验所用的MULTI-SUM数据集、IN-DOMAIN与OUT-OF-DOMAIN的具体定义及评估目的，并补充了四种学习策略和分析性实验。所有内容均有原文段落逐字支持：引用[1]支持三种设置及其评估目的，[6]支持MULTI-SUM数据集及IN/OUT-OF-DOMAIN定义，[2]支持四种学习策略，[3]支持分析性实验。答案将[1]中的'DOMAIN'表述为'IN-DOMAIN'，但[6]明确使用'IN-DOMAIN'一词，且[1]后文提及'IN-DOMAIN setting'，故无实质错误。未发现无依据的额外断言。

citations.quote: 5 Experiment We investigate the effectiveness of the above four strategies under three evaluation settings: DOMAIN, OUT-OF-DOMAIN and CROSS-DATASET. These settings make it possible to explicitly eval- uate models both on the quality of domain-aware text representation and on their adaptation ability to derive reasonable representations in unfamiliar domains.

5.1 Experiment Setup We perform our experiments mainly on our multi- domain MULTI-SUM dataset. Source domains are deﬁned as the ﬁrst ﬁve domains (IN-DOMAIN) in Table 1 and the other domains (OUT-OF- DOMAIN) are totally invisible during training. The evaluation under the IN-DOMAIN setting tests the model ability to learn different domain distribution on a multi-domain set and later OUT-OF-DOMAIN investigates how models perform on unseen do- mains.

Then we re-purpose a multi- domain summarization dataset and verify how the gap between different domains inﬂuences the performance of neural summarization mod- els. Furthermore, we investigate four learning strategies and examine their abilities to deal with the domain shift problem. Experimental results on three different settings show their different characteristics in our new testbed.

3 Analytical Experiment for Domain Shift Domain shift refers to the phenomenon that a model trained on one domain performs poorly on a different domain(Saenko et al., 2010; Gopalan et al., 2011). To clearly verify the existence of do- main shift in the text summarization, we design a simple experiment on MULTI-SUM dataset. Concretely, we take turns choosing one domain and use its training data to train the basic model.
